subject: Acme POC: success criteria, evaluation plan, and rubric
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Acme POC: success criteria, evaluation plan, and rubric

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC plan: 

1) Proposed success criteria (high level)
- Quality: Mean human rating >= 4.5 / 5 on our shared rubric (see attached).
- Safety / hallucination: < 2% critical hallucination rate on labeled set.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 200ms for typical prompts (<=512 tokens).
- Cost: Target token cost less than $0.015 per 1k response tokens (initial target for feasibility).

2) Evaluation plan
- Offline eval: Redwood will run initial offline tests on the labeled sample set you provide (recommended ~1k queries, stratified by intent/content type). We will produce per-intent breakdowns and error examples.
- Online shadow: After offline calibration, we propose a 2-week online shadow (no responses returned to users) to validate live distribution and performance characteristics (cache hit rates, latency under real traffic).

3) Ownership & inputs
- Acme: provide labeled sample set (or 1k-1.5k unlabeled + annotation window), priority intents, and any redaction rules.
- Redwood: run offline evaluation, share full rubric scoring and examples, stand up shadow infrastructure and instrumentation, and provide weekly syncs.

4) Timeline (proposed)
- June 12: Acme to share labeled dataset (or initial 1k sample).
- June 15: Kickoff + environment access & SSO setup.
- June 16–22: Offline eval runs and deliverables (report + per-intent metrics).
- June 23–July 7: Online shadowing period.

Attachments: acme_poc-success-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet of proposed metrics & data spec).

Please confirm the success criteria and timeline or flag any blockers (PII/redaction needs, legal/security preferences). If this looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff for June 15 and send a short SOW / DocuSign for POC credits.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme POC: success criteria, evaluation plan, and rubric

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Labeled examples: We can deliver ~1.2k labeled queries (across 8 intents) but will need to redact PII. Is redaction acceptable for the offline eval?
- Prioritization: Can we prioritize intent A, B, C during the offline run and get per-intent pass/fail?
- Timeline: we prefer a slightly faster offline turnaround if possible — can you compress the offline eval to 3 business days?

Also, curious for more detail on the rubric fields (what exactly are you scoring, and how do you handle partial credit?). If you can share a draft rubric we’ll review before the kickoff.

We’re aligned on a June 15 kickoff — I’ll aim to get the labeled set to you by June 12 and will ask Priya to coordinate the security questionnaire.

Best,
Alex

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC: success criteria, evaluation plan, and rubric

Alex / team — thanks for the note. Quick note on methodology and rubric (attaching a short plan): redwood-eval-plan-v1.pdf

We recommend the following approach: start with an offline eval to calibrate models and thresholds, then run a short shadow period to validate real-traffic characteristics. Concrete rubric fields:
- Accuracy (1–5): correct factual response independent of style.
- Relevance (1–5): degree to which the response answers the user intent.
- Hallucination flag (binary + severity): 0/1 + severity label; counted towards overall critical error rate.
- Completeness (1–5): covers all required items in the prompt or intent specification.
- Latency bucket (pass/fail by p95 target).

Scoring: we map 1–5 to percentage bands and compute a weighted mean (weights can be tuned by Acme; default weights: Accuracy 35%, Relevance 25%, Completeness 20%, Hallucination penalty 15%, Latency 5%). Passing threshold: weighted mean >= 4.5 and hallucination critical rate < 2% on labeled set.

On offline vs online: offline is great for controlled error analysis (allows targeted prompt perturbations). Shadowing reveals user distribution shifts and operational signals (cache behavior, error spikes). For your timeline: we can compress the offline run to 3 business days if the labeled set is available and formatted per the attached spec.

Operational asks for shadowing (high level): request_id in logs, intent tag per request, user-hash (pseudonymized), input/output token counts, and sampling of raw inputs for manual review (with PII redaction options).

—Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC: success criteria, evaluation plan, and rubric

Adding a few instrumentation and security notes from the ops side: 

- Instrumentation: We will provide a shadow ingestion endpoint and a lightweight SDK for event logging. Required fields: request_id, timestamp, intent_tag, user_hash, input_token_count, output_token_count, model_name, model_variant, and a brief metadata blob for context.
- Data retention & privacy: By default Redwood retains logs for 30 days for POC use; we can adjust retention or enable on-premised log delivery if needed. Any PII should be redacted before upload; we can offer automatic PII scrubbers but prefer customer-side redaction where possible.
- Security questionnaire: I’ll send the standard POC security questionnaire (SOC2 / data handling) — please return signed/company responses by June 10 to keep the timeline.

Attachment: shadow-instrumentation-checklist.md (simple checklist of required fields and examples). Happy to hop on a brief technical call during the kickoff to walk through the shadow integration.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference

All — this plan looks good and aligned. Quick confirmations: 
- We will provide the 1.2k labeled dataset (redacted for PII) by EOD June 12.
- Priya will complete the security questionnaire and return by June 10.
- We accept the proposed rubric and weighted scoring; please proceed with the 3-business-day offline run once dataset is received.
- Please send the SOW / DocuSign for the POC credits so procurement can sign off.

Confirming the kickoff for June 15 — 9:00am PT works for our team.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the results.

Best,
Alex
